about: One row per platform. requires = asset ids from scripts/scan.py ASSETS (a|b means either). dr = claimed domain rating (unverified unless verified=yes). steps: claude = Claude does it locally; approve = Claude runs it after an explicit yes (publish, PR, upload); human = the user does it (accounts, payment, DNS, forms, email). see = pointer to the fact's other home instead of steps.

platforms.name: Official MCP Registry
platforms.listing: registry entry; mirrored by Glama, PulseMCP and MCP clients
platforms.link: metadata only; value is downstream distribution
artifacts: server.json (name, title, description, version, remotes[].url or packages[])
package marker: mcpName in package.json, or mcp-name: <name> in the PyPI README
steps: claude: confirm the server is either a published package (npm/PyPI/OCI) or a remote Streamable HTTP URL under remotes
claude: write server.json (mcp-publisher init shape) and the package marker
human: brew install mcp-publisher
human: prove the namespace: mcp-publisher login github (io.github.<user>/*), or for com.yourdomain/* add the DNS TXT record and run mcp-publisher login dns --domain <domain> --private-key <key>
approve: mcp-publisher publish (versions are immutable)
platforms.notes: Publish here before Glama/Smithery: aggregators ingest it. Registry is labeled preview. Thread says DNS-only; the registry docs also allow GitHub namespace login, which needs no domain.

platforms.name: Smithery
artifacts: README badge from Smithery
icon
steps: human: sign in at smithery.ai/new and paste the remote MCP URL
human: if the server takes an API key, add connection parameter apiKey with location header, output as header Authorization (the default query location never reaches your auth)
human: Settings tab: display name, description, homepage, icon, GitHub repo
human: add the smithery-verification TXT record to the root domain
approve: commit the Smithery badge to the repo README
platforms.notes: 2026-11 recheck: URL publish at smithery.ai/new or `smithery mcp publish <url> -n @org/server`; stdio servers ship as an MCPB bundle; serve /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json if the scan can't reach tools; return 401 not 403 so OAuth discovery works; allowlist the SmitheryBot/1.0 user agent.

platforms.name: Glama MCP connectors
artifacts: /.well-known/glama.json on the MCP host (or a TXT record)
tool descriptions that say when to use each tool instead of its siblings
steps: claude: rewrite weak tool descriptions (Glama grades each tool A-F)
claude: write /.well-known/glama.json for the MCP host
human: after the MCP Registry publish (Glama ingests it within about an hour) open the connector page and click Claim ownership
human: Admin -> Test profile: sign in with OAuth or paste an API key, otherwise the listing shows Unhealthy and drops out of search
human: optional second page: Add Server with the public GitHub repo
platforms.notes: Repo listings: glama.json with $schema and maintainers at the repo root (required for org repos). Remote connectors: /.well-known/glama.json, maintainer email must match the Glama account.
